_meta.description: D6 fixtures for langgraph-fastapi / a2ui-recovery (A2UI error recovery)
_meta._note: Backend-owned A2UI (get_a2ui_tools, injectA2UITool=false). NO `context` match field: a real browser (the dojo) does not send x-aimock-context, so context-scoped fixtures would 404 in-browser; the recovery pills' prompts are UNIQUE per framework, so userMessage alone disambiguates. HEAL: seq 0 invalid -> retry -> seq 1 valid -> paints. EXHAUST: invalid every attempt -> exhausts. Mirrors langgraph-python/a2ui-recovery.json. Repeat invocations: the HEAL sequenceIndex variants are followed by a NON-SEQUENCED fallback serving the same valid surface, so once slots 0 and 1 are spent (counters are per-X-Test-Id and never reset; a real browser sends no X-Test-Id) the inner render call still paints instead of falling through to the userMessage-only outer-emit fixture and exhausting. GOTCHAS.md's sanctioned repeat-invocation pattern.

fixtures._comment: HEAL pill - inner render_a2ui repeat-invocation FALLBACK. No sequenceIndex, ordered AFTER the two sequenced variants, serving the SAME valid surface as sequenceIndex 1. Load-bearing: aimock's sequenceIndex counters are bucketed per X-Test-Id and never reset within a bucket, and a real browser sends no X-Test-Id, so slots 0 and 1 are spent by the FIRST heal and every later heal skipped both gates and fell through to the userMessage-only outer-emit fixture below -- which serves generate_a2ui, not render_a2ui, so the recovery loop saw empty_components on all 3 attempts and painted the amber "Couldn't generate the UI" card while the narration still claimed success. With this fallback the first heal still stages invalid->retry->valid and every heal after it paints immediately. This is GOTCHAS.md's sanctioned repeat-invocation pattern (sequenceIndex variants + a non-sequenced fallback ordered after them) and the same stateless shape the EXHAUST pill above/below already uses.
